en: A key term when talking about large language
models is the term token.
Because large language models act on tokens.
They use tokens as input, they use tokens as
output. Now, of course, a large language
model in the end is about getting text as
input and spitting out text as output. But
that text is split up into so-called tokens,
into which a model converts input before it
handles it. And which it then uses for the
output of the computation. So which is the
result of the model, you could say.
Now behind the scenes, these tokens
are converted to IDs. So you can really
think of every token having its own IDs
because when these large language models
were trained, they analyzed pretty much all
the text you can find in the internet. And
they used a tool called a tokenizer, which
they also built themselves. The people that
built the large language model built that
tokenizer tool. And the idea there was that
all these words that make up all that text
are split up into those tokens.
And those words are split up into tokens to
be able to catch more nuances and more
details.
And then every unique token would get a
unique ID. So we're talking about many, many
IDs here because we have all these tokens
for different languages and so on.
And the models then simply were trained to
understand the relation between these
different IDs and therefore between the
different tokens and therefore ultimately
the relation between these different words
or parts of words.
Now tokens matter these days because for
one, it's nice to know what's happening
behind the scenes, but also because when
you're working with these AI models,
you are billed per token, which means you
are paying for the tokens you're sending to
a model and you're paying for the output
tokens. Now, you may not directly be paying
if you have a subscription, but that
subscription then only covers a certain
amount of tokens. And if you're directly
using these models through the APIs, the
application programming interfaces provided
by these model providers, you are indeed
paying per token. That's why this token
concept is really important to understand.
